text:
camila: hey everyone — first day! getting my workstation set up (M1 Mac). stuck on a couple things: asdf python keeps saying \"no such version\" even after `asdf install 3.11.4`, brew complains about openssl when building some wheels, and my ssh agent forwarding to our bastion isn't working. also 1password CLI auth seems to require a session token i can't find. any quick tips or who should I ping?

ben: welcome! :tada: for asdf, run `asdf plugin-list` then `asdf plugin-add python` if missing. also `asdf reshim` after install. if `asdf install` errored, paste the error. for M1 you often need `brew install openssl@1.1` then set env flags before pip building wheels: `export LDFLAGS=\"-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib\"` and `export CPPFLAGS=\"-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include\"`.

katie: adding — for 1password CLI, do `op signin my` (or `op signin --account my`) and it prints an `OP_SESSION_<account>` token. either eval that or add it to your shell env for the session. if you're using direnv, put `export OP_SESSION_my=...` in an `.envrc` guarded by `op` calls, or use `op inject` patterns.

camila: thanks — i didn't realize `asdf plugin-add` was missing. after that `asdf install` still failed with a build error about macOS SDK. shows: \"clang: error: cannot find macro definition file\" when compiling openssl-backed extension.

oliver: try installing the Xcode CLT: `xcode-select --install`. also ensure you have `export SDKROOT=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)` in your shell before building. for some pyexts, `brew reinstall python@3.11` after openssl helps.

ben: ssh agent forwarding — check `~/.ssh/config` for the host entry: `Host bastion
  HostName bastion.redwood.local
  ForwardAgent yes
  User camila` and locally do `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (on mac the `-K` stores in keychain; on newer macOS use `--apple-use-keychain` depending on OpenSSH). then from bastion the agent should be available to hop to internal hosts. you can verify with `ssh -A bastion` and `ssh-add -l` on the bastion.

camila: i tried `ssh-add -K` but `ssh-add -l` returns \"The agent has no identities\" when i'm on the bastion. locally `ssh-add -l` shows the key.

oliver: did you `ssh -A`? also confirm the ssh client version on your mac supports `-K`. run `ssh -V`. if the bastion has `AllowAgentForwarding yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`. if not, ping infra.

infra-bot: Hi Camila — there's an open bastion config change request (REQ-2026) that temporarily disables agent forwarding for some accounts. If you need immediate access, DM @oliver and we can add a temporary exception.

camila: ah ok that explains it — thanks infra-bot and oliver, i'll DM. last quick weirdness: i'm using fish shell and direnv, some env vars from 1password aren't being exported into the devcontainer. any known gotchas?

katie: with fish + direnv, ensure your direnv hooks are fish-compatible (`direnv hook fish` in your `config.fish`). for devcontainers, you'll want to use the `postCreateCommand` to run `op signin` or copy needed session tokens into the container's env. alternatively, use `devcontainer.json` remoteEnv and a short wrapper script that reads `op` and writes files into `.devcontainer/secrets` with restrictive perms.

devex-bot: Onboarding doc: https://intranet.redwood/dev-setup — has a fish section, asdf tips, and a note about OP_SESSION env usage.

camila: awesome — did the plugin-add + xcode CLT + reshim steps and python now installs. hitting the bastion exception with agent-forwarding so DMing oliver. 1password sign-in worked after `op signin` and exporting OP_SESSION var into fish. thanks all :pray: super helpful.

ben: nice! if anything else, ping #devex or drop a note here so we can add missing bits to the onboarding doc. :+1:

camila: will do — appreciate the warm welcome :smile:
